free_tier.stated: 'Enroll in the GitLab for Open Source Program and receive features of GitLab Ultimate ..., including 50,000 compute minutes calculated at a program-specific cost factor.' Quoted from the compute-minutes page: 'Public projects in the GitLab for Open Source program' cost factor '0.5', '1 minute per 2 minutes of job time'. Quoted from the GPU runner page: 'Tier: Premium, Ultimate' with a single machine type of 4 vCPU, 15 GB, 50 GB disk and '1 NVIDIA Tesla T4 (or similar)' at 16 GB GPU memory. The default Linux runner is 2 vCPU / 8 GB / 30 GB; medium is 4 vCPU / 16 GB / 50 GB.

identity_cost.detail: a GitLab.com account that owns a Free-tier group, since personal namespaces are not eligible; every project in the group carries an OSI-approved licence and is publicly visible; the application is a Customers Portal form that is reviewed, and membership is renewed annually

evidence.proved: receive features of GitLab Ultimate including 50,000 compute minutes at a program-specific cost factor; requirements are an OSI-approved licence on every project in the namespace, no profit-seeking, and public visibility; membership must be renewed annually

Free tier namespaces receive 400 compute minutes per month; project-type discount table: public projects in the GitLab for Open Source program cost factor 0.5, public forks of them 0.008, standard projects 1; runner cost factors small 1, medium 2, large 3, xlarge 6, 2xlarge 12, GPU standard 7, macOS M1 6
Tier: Premium, Ultimate; one GPU machine type saas-linux-medium-amd64-gpu-standard at 4 vCPU, 15 GB, 50 GB and one NVIDIA Tesla T4 with 16 GB
saas-linux-small-amd64 is the untagged default at 2 vCPU, 8 GB, 30 GB; medium is 4 vCPU, 16 GB, 50 GB; large and above are Premium and Ultimate only
The default maximum time that jobs can run for is 60 minutes, settable per project between 10 minutes and 1 month
the 0.5 factor was introduced because projects migrating to the OSS plan were using more than 50,000 minutes per month, where 50,000 is the OSS and Ultimate monthly limit
the saas-linux hosted runners run privileged and support Docker-in-Docker
evidence.quote: Runners with any of the `saas-linux-<size>-<architecture>` tags are configured to run in `privileged` mode to support [Docker-in-Docker](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/docker/using_docker_build/#use-docker-in-docker).

notes: The GPU figure rests on one reading the pages do not settle. Usage is job duration / 60 x cost factor, runner type and project type sit in separate tables, and the project table gives public projects in the GitLab for Open Source program a cost factor of 0.5 with no runner qualifier. Read literally, a GPU job also costs 0.5, so 50,000 compute minutes are 100,000 job-minutes, or 1,667 GPU-hours a month. If the programme factor and the GPU runner factor of 7 multiply, 50,000 / 3.5 is 14,285 job-minutes, or 238 GPU-hours. The two readings differ by a factor of seven, and only a job run in an accepted namespace settles it. GPU runners are offered on Premium and Ultimate only, and the grant is Ultimate. The default runner is 2 vCPU and 8 GB, a job on GitLab.com hosted runners times out after 3 hours, and the grant is a monthly pool rather than unlimited time.
